consumer: The frontend map-view renderer, which asks 'what terrain/furniture do I draw at each nearby tile so the player sees the map?' — it SHOWS the value.
scope: a map region — the nearby tiles in the export window around the center, as the player would see/remember them
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_tiles writes raw ctx.m.ter(p).id().str() and ctx.m.furn(p).id().str() per tile — raw map state, NOT a visibility/memory-filtered display view
divergence: A tile that changed while out of the player's sight (e.g. a wall smashed open or terrain altered in fog-of-war): the map view should display the remembered/old terrain (or unknown), but raw ter()/furn() reports the new ground truth, exposing the raw-state answer as wrong for the display consumer.
